# Review — PAN-4259
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — spawn.ts:719 passes `options.effort`, not `launchEffort.effort`, to `createFreshSessionIdentity`, so sessions.json records a stale or overridden effort on tiered work spawns (FR-2)

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-4259-review-48cb8abc
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4259/.pan/review/agent-pan-4259-review-48cb8abc/context.json

## Blocking Findings

### [correctness] Fresh spawn indexes the caller's effort instead of the launch effort — `src/lib/agents/spawn.ts:719`
- Severity: ! (MUST)
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect; in_pr_scope (FR-2, PRD AC-2, issue AC 1 "sessions.json entries record the launch effort"). This confirms the CodeRabbit inline finding on the same line.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: `spawnAgentWithoutConsentClaim` computes
  `const launchEffort = pickLaunchEffort({ effort: options.effort, effortSource: options.effortSource }, singleTierParams);` (line 670).
  `pickLaunchEffort` (`src/lib/agents/launch-effort.ts`) replaces a non-explicit or missing caller effort with the staffed tier effort. The state literal stores `...spawnEffortFields(launchEffort.effort, launchEffort.effortSource)` (line 714) and the launcher gets `effort: launchEffort.effort` (line 819). But the line this PR changed passes `createFreshSessionIdentity(agentId, resolvedHarness, selectedModel, options.effort)` (line 719).
  `resolveSingleWorkTierSpawnParams` (`src/lib/agents/spawn-prep.ts:493`) staffs through `resolveStaffing` "Always Tiered" (PAN-2397) and returns `effort`/`effortSource` for every single-work spawn with a readable plan. The live host config has `tiered_execution.enabled: true`. `createFreshSessionIdentity` only allocates for `launcher-session-id` harnesses, which is claude-code (`packages/contracts/src/harness-behavior.ts`), the default work harness.
- Expected / observed / impact:
  - Expected: the new sessions.json line carries the effort the session actually launched at (`launchEffort.effort`, the same value saved to state.json and sent to `--effort`).
  - Observed (static trace): when the caller passes no effort, `sessionIndexLine` falls back to `recorded.effort` from state.json. That state.json is still the previous launch's file, because `saveAgentStateSync(state)` runs later (line 731) and `agent-<issue>` ids are reused across fresh spawns. So the line records the previous launch's effort. When the caller passes a non-explicit level that the tier overrides, the line records the overridden level.
  - Impact: sessions.json is append-only and the PRD forbids backfill (D6), so the wrong value is permanent. `readLaunchEfforts` checks `byId.get(sessionId)` before the state.json rule, so the wrong indexed value wins over the now-correct state.json for that session's cost rows. For claude-code ≥ 2.1.280 the observed per-record effort masks this in the ledger (D1 rule 1). For older transcripts, and for any record without the field, `pan cost effort` buckets spend under the wrong level.
- Evidence: static trace of `src/lib/agents/spawn.ts` lines 670, 714, 719, 731, 819; `src/lib/agents/launch-effort.ts`; `src/lib/agents/spawn-prep.ts:493-552`; `src/lib/session-history.ts` `sessionIndexLine`/`readLaunchEfforts`; `~/.overdeck/config.yaml` `tiered_execution.enabled: true`. Not reproduced at runtime. History: the PRD (written at `b8853b45510`, 2026-10-03) correctly said `options.effort` at the time. PAN-4257 (`be8b33e49a1`, 2026-10-04) introduced `launchEffort` and was merged into this branch afterward. The merge updated lines 714/819 but left line 719 on `options.effort`. No test covers the tiered path: the new `createFreshSessionIdentity` test passes effort directly, and `restart-effort.test.ts` covers only the recovery path.
- Fix: change line 719 to `createFreshSessionIdentity(agentId, resolvedHarness, selectedModel, launchEffort.effort)`. Same line, no file-size growth. Add a test showing that a staffed single-work spawn writes the same effort to the new sessions.json line as to state.json; it can use the existing spawn test harness with a tier that staffs a different effort than the caller's non-explicit one. Note in the PRD (W2 step 2) that `launchEffort.effort` replaces `options.effort` now that PAN-4257 has landed. The `spawnRun` path (line 369, `effort: options.effort`) is consistent: `spawnRunWithoutConsentClaim` stores `options.effort` in its own state (line 234) and receives the already-picked `slotEffort` from its caller, so it needs no change.

## Non-blocking Findings

- ~ `src/lib/costs/prime-agent-collector.ts`: `readLaunchEfforts(agentId)` runs inside the per-session-file loop, so it re-reads sessions.json and state.json once per file instead of once per agent. The codex and pi collectors memoize per agent. This is a small, bounded deviation from NFR-3 ("once per agent per reconcile pass"). Memoize it by `agentId` the same way.
- ? `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/chat/effortChip.ts` `formatEffortLabel` uses `source in EFFORT_SOURCE_LABELS`, which also matches prototype keys. The server writes only `EffortSource` values from state.json, so nothing reaches this today. Recorded for completeness only.
- Scope: `tests/unit/lib/access-tokens.test.ts` fixes a 1-in-16 false-pass assertion that is unrelated to PAN-4259. It is harmless and correct, but outside the issue's scope.
- Other session-index writers (`activity.ts` rotation/recovered, codex/kimi capture, acp host, muse launcher, external registry) pass no effort. They get it through the `recorded.effort` state.json fallback, because they run after state.json exists, which satisfies FR-1. Only the two pre-save launcher writers needed explicit effort. Recovery passes it correctly; spawn.ts:719 does not (blocker above).

### Dimensions
- Correctness: one blocker (spawn.ts:719). The rest of the data path traces end to end: launch → sessions.json → `readLaunchEfforts` → reconcilers/collectors → both write doors and the archive → report. Legacy rows (NULL / missing key) parse (NFR-1).
- Security: no new trust boundary. `getEffortRollup` binds `issueId` as a parameter; the `WHERE` fragment is a constant. The new frontend field is rendered as text.
- Performance: one lookup per agent per pass, except prime-agent (advisory). The report runs one GROUP BY query. The directory change reads already-loaded state.
- Requirements/UX: see the matrix. Non-goals respected: no `CostResolver.byEffort`, no HTTP route, no strike.ts change, no effort defaults, no backfill, no `effortSource` on sessions.json or cost rows.
